text:
Erin Lowe: Quick question from recruiting: candidate asked whether domestic partners are eligible for HSA-compatible medical plans and if that affects HSA contributions. They live together and are on partners employer plan but interviewing as single.

Marcus Chen: Domestic partners are eligible for Redwood benefits only for medical if theyre registered under our dependent rules. HSA eligibility depends on whether they are enrolled in a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) through us. If partner is on their employer HDHP, candidate remains HSA-eligible only if they are NOT enrolled in a non-HDHP elsewhere. Complicated but standard.

Erin Lowe: Ok, so in offer language: "HSA eligibility requires enrollment in our HDHP and no concurrent non-HDHP coverage." Good to have that exact phrasing.

Samira Ali: Note for onboarding: ask candidate during benefits intake if theyre covered elsewhere. BrightPlan shows "HSA eligible" flag based on election, but we need HR to confirm before payroll sets up pre-tax HSA deductions.

BenefitsBot: Reminder: 2025 HSA contribution limits (pre-tax): $3,850 individual / $7,750 family. Catch-up $1,000 for 55+. Payroll will cap per IRS limits; excess contributions are returned per BrightPlan process.

Erin Lowe: Another candidate question: can employees take a 401(k) loan shortly after hire, or is there a waiting period? Recruiting wants to give an honest answer.

Marcus Chen: Plan permits loans after 1 year of participation or after 1,000 hours of service (whichever meets plan rules). If someone rolls over funds in, loan availability may vary. Recommend we say "loans subject to plan rules; typically available after 12 months of participation."

Samira Ali: Also include note: loans reduce vestable account balance for withdrawal purposes and repayments are payroll-deducted. For leaves of absence, outstanding loans go to repayment terms per plan; if they default it counts as distribution and taxable.

Gita (Payroll): Adding payroll detail: if someone takes leave, we attempt payroll deduction but if employer stops deductions we follow plan default (may go to amortization or deemed distribution). Benefits team will notify payroll before LOA to set loan handling.

Erin Lowe: Perfect. Last hiring ops nuance: if a new hire requests pretax HSA contributions starting with first paycheck but their paperwork arrives late, can we do a retroactive HSA deposit? Candidate cares about using funds immediately for a medical bill.

Marcus Chen: We can only make pre-tax payroll elections effective for payrolls after election processed. If missed, employee can do an HSA contribution outside payroll and claim it on taxes (form 8889) or BrightPlan may allow an employee-directed after-tax adjustment if within calendar year; but payroll cannot reclassify previous net pay after reporting.

Samira Ali: Practical guidance for recruiting: "To have HSA funds in first check, ensure benefits election + signed offer are submitted to payroll at least 10 business days before start; otherwise advise candidate about alternative: direct HSA contribution and tax deduction."

BenefitsBot: Helpful link: HSA FAQ internal doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PeopleOps/pages/HSA-FAQ (internal).

Erin Lowe: Great, I'll update the hiring checklist and offer packet language with these bullets and the loan caveat. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
